bougie:Maison Jeunet par Steven Naessens.name: Maison Jeunet par Steven Naessens — Château de Germigney
bougie:Maison Jeunet par Steven Naessens.label: ★★ · RELAIS & CHÂTEAUX
bougie:Maison Jeunet par Steven Naessens.hook: The historic Arbois ★★ relocated to the Château de Germigney, both stars intact
bougie:Maison Jeunet par Steven Naessens.text: The historic Arbois ★★ relocated to the Château de Germigney, both stars intact EUR 95-130 menu ESSENTIAL Dinner Jean-Paul Jeunet retired; Steven Naessens, his Flemish protégé, took the kitchen and the name to the Château de Germigney at Port-Lesney in November 2021. Two Michelin stars confirmed at the 2022 Cognac ceremony and held through 2026. Signature: cromesquis of Morbier and Morteau; snails in Savagnin broth; Bresse poultry with Vin Jaune and morel sauce; hare royale. Sommelier Laurie Derouard pours Domaine de la Pinte Savagnin alongside the classics. Menu €95 / à la carte ~€110. Closed February + October school holidays. Where Port-Lesney — 30 km north of Lons

bougie:Château du Mont Joly — Sampans.name: Château du Mont Joly — Sampans
bougie:Château du Mont Joly — Sampans.label: ★ · MOF
bougie:Château du Mont Joly — Sampans.hook: ★ held 20 consecutive years · Chef Romuald Fassenet (Meilleur Ouvrier de France 2004)
bougie:Château du Mont Joly — Sampans.text: ★ held 20 consecutive years · Chef Romuald Fassenet (Meilleur Ouvrier de France 2004) EUR fine-dining (gastro Fri-Sat) ESSENTIAL Dinner 18th-century pink-façade manor with Italianate columns and views over the Saône valley; 7 rooms. Fassenet's wife (daughter of winegrowers) is the sommelier. Signature: smoked eel; hand-dived scallops; poularde de Bresse with Vin Jaune + morels + Château-Chalon sauce. The gastronomic menu is served only Friday evening to Saturday (3 services); bistro the rest of the week. Where Sampans — 40 km north (near Dole)

bougie:La Chaumière — Dole.name: La Chaumière — Dole
bougie:La Chaumière — Dole.label: ★ + BIB
bougie:La Chaumière — Dole.hook: ★ since 2008 + Bib Gourmand on the bistro side · Chef Laurent Barberot
bougie:La Chaumière — Dole.text: ★ since 2008 + Bib Gourmand on the bistro side · Chef Laurent Barberot EUR fine-dining gastro / bistro accessible ESSENTIAL gastro / RECOMMENDED bistro Dinner Laurent Barberot (Plaza Athénée, La Pyramide Vienne, La Côte d'Or Saulieu, Le Clos des Sens Annecy) took the helm from Joël Césari and held the star through transition. Seasonal tasting menu with Jura accents — smoked eel, Bresse poultry, Jura cheeses. Gastronomic Fri eve + Sat lunch & dinner only; bistro the rest of the week. Where Dole — 40 km north

dish:Poularde de Bresse au Vin Jaune et.name: Poularde de Bresse au Vin Jaune et morilles
dish:Poularde de Bresse au Vin Jaune et.label: THE CATHEDRAL DISH
dish:Poularde de Bresse au Vin Jaune et.hook: The plate that explains why the region exists
dish:Poularde de Bresse au Vin Jaune et.text: The plate that explains why the region exists EUR 45-80 ESSENTIAL Dinner Free-range AOC Bresse hen — "blue legs," four-month feeding regime — poached in Vin Jaune with dried morels and cream. The chemistry: Vin Jaune's sotolon (120–268 µg/L) binds the free glutamate of dried morels and the fat of the blue-footed bird. Pure chemistry at table. Where Jeunet · Mont Joly · La Petite Auberge

dish:Comté in three ages (12 / 18 / 24 /.name: Comté in three ages (12 / 18 / 24 / 36 months)
dish:Comté in three ages (12 / 18 / 24 /.label: THE CHEESE
dish:Comté in three ages (12 / 18 / 24 /.text: Vertical tasting, side by side EUR 8-15 / 100g range WALK-IN All day France's #1 AOP cheese, 61,000 tonnes in 2024. Made only from Montbéliarde (95 %) and Simmental française (5 %) milk — 400 L per 40 kg wheel. Tasting three ages reveals the curve: 12-month milky and fruity; 18-month nutty; 24-month grainy and saline; 36-month dry, caramel, tyrosine crystals crunching. Marcel Petite's Fort Saint-Antoine (1879–82, 1,100 m altitude, 100,000 wheels) is where the longest agings happen. Where Fromagerie Vagne · Maison du Comté Poligny

dish:Saucisse de Morteau IGP.name: Saucisse de Morteau IGP
dish:Saucisse de Morteau IGP.label: CHARCUTERIE
dish:Saucisse de Morteau IGP.hook: Sealed by a wooden plug, 48h+ in a tuyé
dish:Saucisse de Morteau IGP.text: Sealed by a wooden plug, 48h+ in a tuyé EUR 6-12 / piece WALK-IN Lunch / Dinner Pork sausage IGP-protected since 2010, minimum 40 mm diameter, coarse-ground, sealed at one end with the unique cheville (wooden plug) — the legal visual identifier. Smoked minimum 48 hours and often up to 7 days in a tuyé , the massive 12–15-m pyramid chimney of Haut-Doubs farmhouses, over conifer and juniper sawdust. Cook in barely-simmering water, never pierced, for 45 min. With lentils, or in cancoillotte, or in a Morbier morbiflette. Where the market · La Finette · every serious tasca

dish:Pochouse jurassienne.name: Pochouse jurassienne
dish:Pochouse jurassienne.label: TRADITIONAL
dish:Pochouse jurassienne.hook: Freshwater fish stew — the Jura's bouillabaisse
dish:Pochouse jurassienne.text: Freshwater fish stew — the Jura's bouillabaisse EUR 18-26 WALK-IN Dinner The Jurassien version of bouillabaisse, with freshwater fish from the Doubs and the Loue: pike, perch, eel, tench, sometimes burbot. Cooked in white Jura wine with garlic, onions, lardons, cream; served over toasted bread. Best at La Table de Perraud . Where La Table de Perraud · Le Bistrot des Marronniers

dish:Cancoillotte.name: Cancoillotte
dish:Cancoillotte.label: TRADITIONAL
dish:Cancoillotte.hook: Melted soft cheese with garlic and white wine — the peasant pour
dish:Cancoillotte.text: Melted soft cheese with garlic and white wine — the peasant pour EUR 3-7 / jar WALK-IN All day Franche-Comté's peasant cheese — under 15 % fat, made from metton (skim-milk curd) melted with butter, water and garlic or Jura white wine. Sold cold in jars; warmed and poured over potatoes, into omelettes, on Morteau sausage. Effectively impossible to find outside the region at its best. Where every market · every traditional table

dish:Mont d'Or AOP — la boîte chaude.name: Mont d'Or AOP — la boîte chaude
dish:Mont d'Or AOP — la boîte chaude.label: CHEESE
dish:Mont d'Or AOP — la boîte chaude.hook: Spruce-barked, available only October to early May
dish:Mont d'Or AOP — la boîte chaude.text: Spruce-barked, available only October to early May EUR 12-20 WALK-IN Lunch / Dinner Seasonal washed-rind cheese, available only from late September to early May, when Montbéliarde cows come down from summer pasture and milk volumes drop too low for Comté. Each wheel is encircled by a sangle of Norway-spruce cambium — the resinous, forest-floor note in the cheese. Sold in a spruce wooden box. At peak, served as la boîte chaude : oven-warmed in the box, scooped onto potatoes with Morteau sausage and charcuterie. Where the markets · every fromagerie in season

dish:Bleu de Gex Haut-Jura AOP.name: Bleu de Gex Haut-Jura AOP
dish:Bleu de Gex Haut-Jura AOP.label: CHEESE
dish:Bleu de Gex Haut-Jura AOP.hook: France's first cow's-milk blue AOC (1977), made by monks since the 13th c.
dish:Bleu de Gex Haut-Jura AOP.text: France's first cow's-milk blue AOC (1977), made by monks since the 13th c. EUR 6-10 / 100g WALK-IN All day Mountain blue cheese from the upper Jura valleys, made from raw Montbéliarde or Simmental milk; aged on spruce boards. First cow's-milk blue to receive a French AOC (1977; AOP 1996). Documented production since the 13th century by the monks of the Abbey of Condat. 6–9 kg wheel, whitish floury rind, blue veins, surprisingly mild fruit-and-vanilla character. Where Haut-Jura · the markets · Fromagerie Vagne

drink:Vin Jaune — the cathedral wine.name: Vin Jaune — the cathedral wine
drink:Vin Jaune — the cathedral wine.label: WINE
drink:Vin Jaune — the cathedral wine.hook: Savagnin · 6 yrs 3 mos under voile · 62 cl clavelin
drink:Vin Jaune — the cathedral wine.text: Savagnin · 6 yrs 3 mos under voile · 62 cl clavelin EUR 35-90 / clavelin ESSENTIAL at table Dinner Grown on blue marls, made from Savagnin only, aged 6 years 3 months under a voile of yeast in a barrel left unfilled — bottled in a 62 cl clavelin , the volume that supposedly remains after evaporation. The voile is thinner than Sherry flor, lets a little oxygen through, thrives at lower minimum alcohol (~13 % vs 15–15.5 %). It produces sotolon (3-hydroxy-4,5-dimethyl-2(5H)-furanone, first isolated from fenugreek 1975) at 120–268 µg/L — the molecule of curry, walnut, maple syrup. Pair with the Bresse poularde + morels (the free glutamate amplifies sotolon) or 30-month Comté. Houses: Macle (Château-Chalon), Tissot (Arbois), Ganevat (Rotalier), Overnoy/Houillon (Pupillin), Domaine de la Pinte (Arbois). Where Château-Chalon · Arbois · L'Étoile · Côtes du Jura

drink:Savagnin — the genealogical centre.name: Savagnin — the genealogical centre of European white wine
drink:Savagnin — the genealogical centre.label: WINE
drink:Savagnin — the genealogical centre.hook: Parent of Sauvignon Blanc, Chenin Blanc, Grüner Veltliner · = Traminer blanc
drink:Savagnin — the genealogical centre.text: Parent of Sauvignon Blanc, Chenin Blanc, Grüner Veltliner · = Traminer blanc EUR 18-45 / bottle ESSENTIAL Dinner Vinified two ways. Ouillé (topped-up): fresh, mineral, like a southern Burgundian Chardonnay but with more salt. Sous voile : oxidative, walnut and curry. DNA work (UC Davis / INRA, 1999) confirmed Savagnin = Traminer blanc, and that it is the parent of Sauvignon Blanc, Chenin Blanc, Grüner Veltliner and Verdelho, and grandparent of Cabernet Sauvignon (via Sauvignon × Cabernet Franc). Gewürztraminer is its musqué mutation. The most genealogically central grape in European viticulture, planted on 0.0001 of European vineyard area. Where everywhere in the Jura

drink:Poulsard / Ploussard — the palest.name: Poulsard / Ploussard — the palest red in France
drink:Poulsard / Ploussard — the palest.label: WINE
drink:Poulsard / Ploussard — the palest.hook: Translucent, low tannin, high acid — serve at 12-14 °C
drink:Poulsard / Ploussard — the palest.text: Translucent, low tannin, high acid — serve at 12-14 °C EUR 18-40 / bottle RECOMMENDED Lunch / Dinner Indigenous Jura red. Pale orange-ruby, low tannin, cherry-cranberry fruit, high acid. Pupillin is the world capital — local signage calls it la capitale mondiale du Ploussard . Pair with Morteau or Montbéliard sausage, or with Morbier. Serve lightly chilled. The Overnoy/Houillon expressions are the world reference; the Fruitière Vinicole de Pupillin pours an accessible village wine; Tissot Singulier on the entry side. Where Pupillin · Arbois

drink:Trousseau — the firm Jura red.name: Trousseau — the firm Jura red
drink:Trousseau — the firm Jura red.label: WINE
drink:Trousseau — the firm Jura red.hook: Iron tannin, black-cherry fruit — the serious red
drink:Trousseau — the firm Jura red.text: Iron tannin, black-cherry fruit — the serious red EUR 22-55 / bottle RECOMMENDED Dinner Indigenous Jura red, firmer than Poulsard — deeper colour, more tannin, black-cherry and iron notes. Serve at 14–16 °C. Pair with 18-month Comté (the crystalline nuttiness meets the wine's mineral backbone) and with game and mushroom dishes. Where Arbois · Montigny-lès-Arsures

drink:Vin de Paille — the straw wine.name: Vin de Paille — the straw wine
drink:Vin de Paille — the straw wine.label: WINE
drink:Vin de Paille — the straw wine.hook: Grapes raisined 3 months on straw before pressing
drink:Vin de Paille — the straw wine.text: Grapes raisined 3 months on straw before pressing EUR 35-65 / 37.5 cl RECOMMENDED Dessert Sweet wine made from grapes (Savagnin, Chardonnay, Poulsard) raisined on straw mats for a minimum of three months before pressing — the dehydration concentrates sugars to ~14.5 % alcohol. Aged in barrel 3 years before release. With Comté, with chocolate, or as a meditation pour after. Where Arbois · L'Étoile · Côtes du Jura

drink:Macvin · Crémant · Marc du Jura.name: Macvin · Crémant · Marc du Jura
drink:Macvin · Crémant · Marc du Jura.label: APÉRITIF & DIGESTIF
drink:Macvin · Crémant · Marc du Jura.hook: The three product AOCs — apéritif, sparkling, digestif
drink:Macvin · Crémant · Marc du Jura.text: The three product AOCs — apéritif, sparkling, digestif EUR 14-35 / bottle WALK-IN Apéritif / All day / Digestif Macvin du Jura (AOC since 14 November 1991) — the medieval mistelle of 2/3 grape must + 1/3 Marc du Jura, ~16 % alcohol, sweet, served as the Jura apéritif. Crémant du Jura — bottle-fermented sparkling, Chardonnay-led, the Jura's everyday bubble. Marc du Jura — amber pomace brandy aged in oak, the formal seventh AOC, the digestif. Where every cellar · the Caveau des Jacobins

drink:The 7 Jura appellations.name: The 7 Jura appellations
drink:The 7 Jura appellations.label: TERROIR
drink:The 7 Jura appellations.hook: Arbois · Château-Chalon · Côtes du Jura · L'Étoile + Macvin · Crémant · Marc
drink:The 7 Jura appellations.text: Arbois · Château-Chalon · Côtes du Jura · L'Étoile + Macvin · Crémant · Marc — — — Arbois (~800 ha, all styles, France's first AOC gazette 15 May 1936); Château-Chalon (~50 ha, Vin Jaune only, four communes); Côtes du Jura (the broad regional, all styles); L'Étoile (~83 ha, white only, named for star-shaped crinoid fossils); plus three product AOCs — Macvin, Crémant, Marc. Total Jura vineyard: ~1,950 ha, 230 wineries, 11 million bottles a year. 5 principal grapes (Savagnin, Chardonnay, Pinot Noir, Poulsard, Trousseau). Where the slope

music:La Percée du Vin Jaune.name: La Percée du Vin Jaune
music:La Percée du Vin Jaune.label: FESTIVAL
music:La Percée du Vin Jaune.hook: 31 January – 1 February 2026 · 28th edition · 32,000+ visitors · Europe's largest rural wine gathering
music:La Percée du Vin Jaune.text: 31 January – 1 February 2026 · 28th edition · 32,000+ visitors · Europe's largest rural wine gathering Founded in 1997 by vigneron Bernard Badoz to open the new vintage of Vin Jaune. Rotates through Jura wine communes on the first weekend of February. The 2026 edition (after a 2025 break) was redesigned and hosted in Lons-le-Saunier on 31 January and 1 February 2026, drawing over 32,000 visitors. The percée ceremony breaks the first barrel of the new vintage (2019 in 2026) at the opening. Tastings at hundreds of stalls; the centre of every Jura calendar. Where rotating Jura wine commune — 2026 in Lons-le-Saunier

music:Festival de Musique du Haut-Jura.name: Festival de Musique du Haut-Jura
music:Festival de Musique du Haut-Jura.label: FESTIVAL
music:Festival de Musique du Haut-Jura.hook: Late spring / early summer · classical music in rural Jura settings
music:Festival de Musique du Haut-Jura.text: Late spring / early summer · classical music in rural Jura settings Annual chamber-music and recital festival across Haut-Jura villages — abbey churches, castle courtyards, smaller halls. The Jura's classical music set-piece. 2026 programme published in spring on festival-musique-haut-jura.fr. Where Saint-Claude, Lons, Arbois — annual rotation

music:Besançon — La Rodia SMAC.name: Besançon — La Rodia SMAC
music:Besançon — La Rodia SMAC.label: ELECTRONIC
music:Besançon — La Rodia SMAC.hook: The regional SMAC for current music · the closest electronic programme to Lons
music:Besançon — La Rodia SMAC.text: The regional SMAC for current music · the closest electronic programme to Lons Besançon's La Rodia is the Franche-Comté SMAC — 600-cap, year-round programme of rock, hip-hop, electronic and world music. Closer than Lyon (which is a longer 1h30 south to Le Sucre , the rooftop on La Sucrière). For Nuits Sonores (mid-May in Lyon) the trip is worth the drive. The Jura itself has none of this. Where Besançon — 1 h north

music:Arbois & Pupillin — the natural-wi.name: Arbois & Pupillin — the natural-wine festivals
music:Arbois & Pupillin — the natural-wi.label: PILGRIMAGE
music:Arbois & Pupillin — the natural-wi.hook: The Jura is a world capital of natural wine — the dates the global scene comes here
music:Arbois & Pupillin — the natural-wi.text: The Jura is a world capital of natural wine — the dates the global scene comes here Not a music festival but a cultural one. Arbois and Pupillin are pilgrimage destinations for natural-wine drinkers globally. The Percée du Vin Jaune is the formal anchor; through the year, the Jeudis du Vin in Arbois, open-cellar weekends (Caves Ouvertes), and the Foire Comtoise des Vins du Jura all bring international wine pilgrims to the town. The Caves Ouvertes weekends are when even the allocation-only houses (Overnoy, Ganevat) sometimes open. Where Arbois · Pupillin

culture:Maison natale de Rouget de Lisle.name: Maison natale de Rouget de Lisle
culture:Maison natale de Rouget de Lisle.label: BIRTH HOUSE
culture:Maison natale de Rouget de Lisle.hook: Plaque + courtyard with a centenarian tilleul · Bartholdi statue 1882 on the Place
culture:Maison natale de Rouget de Lisle.text: Plaque + courtyard with a centenarian tilleul · Bartholdi statue 1882 on the Place free (exterior) WALK-IN Afternoon The composer of La Marseillaise was born here on 10 May 1760. He wrote the anthem in Strasbourg in April 1792. The statue of him on Place de la Liberté is by Frédéric-Auguste Bartholdi (1882) — the same sculptor who, three years later, would deliver the Statue of Liberty to New York. The courtyard inside the birth house holds a centenarian tilleul (lime tree) that flowers in May. Where 24 rue du Commerce, Lons

culture:Maison de la Vache qui Rit.name: Maison de la Vache qui Rit
culture:Maison de la Vache qui Rit.label: MUSEUM
culture:Maison de la Vache qui Rit.hook: The world's most recognised processed-cheese brand was born here
culture:Maison de la Vache qui Rit.text: The world's most recognised processed-cheese brand was born here EUR 8-12 WALK-IN All day One of the most internationally recognised food brands in the world was invented in Lons-le-Saunier (population 17,000) by Léon Bel in 1921. The painter Benjamin Rabier drew the laughing red cow in 1923 — a logo refined but never essentially changed since. The museum traces the brand's century of design, advertising, and global distribution. The cheese itself is technically a fromage fondu, distantly related to Comté processed-cheese byproducts. Where Lons — central

culture:Église des Cordeliers.name: Église des Cordeliers
culture:Église des Cordeliers.label: CHURCH
culture:Église des Cordeliers.text: Plain Cordelier rule, ducal tombs free WALK-IN Morning 13th-century Franciscan foundation; the dukes of Chalon-Arlay are buried here. Sober Cordelier architecture; reliquaries and 18th-c. funerary monuments inside. Almost always empty. Where Lons centre

culture:Église Saint-Désiré + Merovingia.name: Église Saint-Désiré + Merovingian crypt
culture:Église Saint-Désiré + Merovingia.label: ROMANESQUE
culture:Église Saint-Désiré + Merovingia.hook: Ask the keeper to see the crypt
culture:Église Saint-Désiré + Merovingia.text: Ask the keeper to see the crypt free WALK-IN Morning 11th-century Romanesque church on the site of a Merovingian sanctuary. In the crypt, the 6th-century stone sarcophagus of Saint Désiré — patron of the city — remains intact. The keeper opens the crypt on request. The earliest physical layer of Lons. Where Lons centre

culture:Musée d'Archéologie du Jura.name: Musée d'Archéologie du Jura
culture:Musée d'Archéologie du Jura.label: MUSEUM
culture:Musée d'Archéologie du Jura.hook: 5,000-year-old wooden tools preserved by lake mud
culture:Musée d'Archéologie du Jura.text: 5,000-year-old wooden tools preserved by lake mud EUR 3-5 WALK-IN Afternoon Jura archaeological collections: prehistoric, Gallo-Roman, medieval. The standout: artefacts from the Néolithique lacustre sites around Lac de Chalain — wooden tools, textiles, organic remains preserved in the lake mud for 5,000+ years. Pre-Iron Age salt-evaporation evidence also displayed. Where Lons — Place Philibert de Chalon

culture:Saline Royale d'Arc-et-Senans.name: Saline Royale d'Arc-et-Senans
culture:Saline Royale d'Arc-et-Senans.label: UNESCO
culture:Saline Royale d'Arc-et-Senans.hook: Ledoux's semicircular ideal-city, brine from 21.25 km away by saumoduc
culture:Saline Royale d'Arc-et-Senans.text: Ledoux's semicircular ideal-city, brine from 21.25 km away by saumoduc EUR 13-15 WALK-IN All day Claude-Nicolas Ledoux (1736–1806) designed the saltworks as a semicircular ideal-city around the Director's House at the focal point — a fusion of Enlightenment rationalism and industrial function. Construction 1775, operations 1779–1895. UNESCO 1982; the Salines de Salins-les-Bains (source of the brine) added to the listing 29 June 2009. The 21.25-km saumoduc — wooden pipeline replaced with cast iron from 1782 — carried concentrated brine through the Chaux forest, where firewood for evaporation was abundant. June–October Festival des Jardins. Where Arc-et-Senans — 25 km east

culture:Baume-les-Messieurs.name: Baume-les-Messieurs
culture:Baume-les-Messieurs.label: ABBEY · VILLAGE
culture:Baume-les-Messieurs.hook: 9th-c. abbey at the foot of a karst amphitheatre
culture:Baume-les-Messieurs.text: 9th-c. abbey at the foot of a karst amphitheatre EUR 5-8 abbey · free village WALK-IN All day Benedictine abbey founded in 869, set at the foot of a vast karst cirque carved by the Dard river. The village clusters under sheer cliffs; the abbey church has a 16th-c. Flemish polyptych. The cirque trail climbs to the source of the Dard from grottoes — an easy 90-min walk. Officially classified one of France's Plus Beaux Villages . Where 15 km east of Lons — cliff-cirque village

culture:Cascades du Hérisson.name: Cascades du Hérisson
culture:Cascades du Hérisson.label: NATURAL
culture:Cascades du Hérisson.hook: L'Éventail (65 m) · Le Grand Saut (60 m) · the climb takes 3-4 hours
culture:Cascades du Hérisson.text: L'Éventail (65 m) · Le Grand Saut (60 m) · the climb takes 3-4 hours free (parking EUR 7) WALK-IN All day Seven waterfalls along 3.5 km of trail rising 255 m through the Hérisson valley. L'Éventail (the Fan, 65 m) is the first; Le Grand Saut (60 m) the climax. Best in spring after snowmelt. Allow 3–4 h for the round trip from Doucier. The Cirque de Ladoye and the Belvédère des 4 Lacs are nearby — combine for a full Jura plateau day. Where Ménétrux-en-Joux — 30 km east

work:Parc des Bains & Source Salée.name: Parc des Bains & Source Salée
work:Parc des Bains & Source Salée.label: PARK
work:Parc des Bains & Source Salée.hook: Plane-tree park, 1900 bandstand, the brine spring still at ~300 g/L
work:Parc des Bains & Source Salée.text: Plane-tree park, 1900 bandstand, the brine spring still at ~300 g/L 5-ha park with mature plane trees, an 1900 bandstand, and the Source Salée pool — brine still at 300 g of salt per litre. Where the salt-worker town meets the thermal town. Where Lons — central

work:Médiathèque de Lons-le-Saunier.name: Médiathèque de Lons-le-Saunier
work:Médiathèque de Lons-le-Saunier.label: LIBRARY
work:Médiathèque de Lons-le-Saunier.text: Quiet reading rooms, free Wi-Fi The municipal library — public, free, with reading rooms, periodicals, working spaces. The civilian alternative when the café is too noisy. Where Lons centre

work:Café de la Comédie.name: Café de la Comédie
work:Café de la Comédie.label: CAFÉ
work:Café de la Comédie.text: Terrace under the 1840 theatre's colonnade The café terrace facing the neoclassical theatre — the best free seat in town on a market morning, with Pelen pastries available three minutes away on rue Blaise Pascal. Where Place de la Comédie

work:Rue du Commerce arcades.name: Rue du Commerce arcades
work:Rue du Commerce arcades.label: ARCADES
work:Rue du Commerce arcades.hook: 146 m of medieval golden-stone arcades — Franche-Comté's only arcaded street
work:Rue du Commerce arcades.text: 146 m of medieval golden-stone arcades — Franche-Comté's only arcaded street Walk the 146 m of arcades early in the morning when the stone catches the first light. No other street like this in Franche-Comté. Where Lons centre

events:La Percée du Vin Jaune 2026 — Lon.name: La Percée du Vin Jaune 2026 — Lons-le-Saunier
events:La Percée du Vin Jaune 2026 — Lon.label: WINE FESTIVAL
events:La Percée du Vin Jaune 2026 — Lon.hook: 31 January – 1 February 2026 · 28th edition · Lons hosted · 32,000+ visitors
events:La Percée du Vin Jaune 2026 — Lon.text: 31 January – 1 February 2026 · 28th edition · Lons hosted · 32,000+ visitors Founded in 1997 by vigneron Bernard Badoz, the Percée rotates through Jura wine villages on the first weekend of February to open the new Vin Jaune vintage. After a 2025 break, the 2026 edition was redesigned and hosted in Lons-le-Saunier : 31 January and 1 February. Over 32,000 visitors. Europe's largest rural wine gathering. The 2026 edition opened the 2019 vintage.

events:Festival de Musique du Haut-Jura.name: Festival de Musique du Haut-Jura
events:Festival de Musique du Haut-Jura.label: MUSIC FESTIVAL
events:Festival de Musique du Haut-Jura.hook: Late spring / early summer 2026 — rotating venues
events:Festival de Musique du Haut-Jura.text: Late spring / early summer 2026 — rotating venues Chamber-music festival across Haut-Jura villages, abbey churches, castle courtyards. The Jura's classical-music annual. Programme on festival-musique-haut-jura.fr — usually announced in spring.

events:Festival Idéklic — Moirans-en-Mon.name: Festival Idéklic — Moirans-en-Montagne
events:Festival Idéklic — Moirans-en-Mon.label: FAMILY
events:Festival Idéklic — Moirans-en-Mon.hook: July 2026 · 30+ years of children's performing arts
events:Festival Idéklic — Moirans-en-Mon.text: July 2026 · 30+ years of children's performing arts International children's performing-arts festival in Moirans-en-Montagne (45 km south, the toy-making capital of France). Theatre, dance, circus, workshops. Long-running and serious — not a tourist event.

events:Livres dans la Boucle — Besançon.name: Livres dans la Boucle — Besançon (1 h)
events:Livres dans la Boucle — Besançon.label: LITERARY
events:Livres dans la Boucle — Besançon.hook: Mid-September 2026 · 200+ authors on the Granvelle promenade
events:Livres dans la Boucle — Besançon.text: Mid-September 2026 · 200+ authors on the Granvelle promenade Besançon's major literary festival — held on the Granvelle promenade in mid-September, with around 200 French and international authors, readings, meetings, signing tables, debates. Free entry. The cultural day-trip from Lons.

events:The Thursday market — the biggest.name: The Thursday market — the biggest in the Jura
events:The Thursday market — the biggest.label: WEEKLY
events:The Thursday market — the biggest.hook: Every Thursday · Place du 11 Novembre + Place de Verdun
events:The Thursday market — the biggest.text: Every Thursday · Place du 11 Novembre + Place de Verdun Lons's anchor weekly market — the largest in the department. Place du 11 Novembre carries manufactured goods all day; Place de Verdun the food morning. Producers from the Haut-Jura plateau and the Bresse plain. The Saturday market (Cours Sully morning) and Wednesday producers' market (Place du 11 Novembre 17h–19h30) complete the cycle.

events:Foire de Comté — Poligny.name: Foire de Comté — Poligny
events:Foire de Comté — Poligny.label: GASTRONOMY
events:Foire de Comté — Poligny.hook: Autumn 2026 — annual Comté festival in the AOP capital
events:Foire de Comté — Poligny.text: Autumn 2026 — annual Comté festival in the AOP capital Poligny — capital of Comté — hosts its annual Foire each autumn: producer stalls, vertical tastings, tuyé demonstrations, Marcel Petite ages on display. Dates published late summer on the CIGC site.

events:Flowering on the Jura slope.name: Flowering on the Jura slope
events:Flowering on the Jura slope.label: THE VINE YEAR
events:Flowering on the Jura slope.hook: Late May into June — the slope sets its harvest
events:Flowering on the Jura slope.text: Late May into June — the slope sets its harvest Not an organised event but a natural one worth timing a visit to. In the last days of May and into June, Savagnin and Chardonnay flower on the blue marls; roughly 100 days later they are picked. The Revermont is at its greenest.

walks:Rue du Commerce arcades at dawn.name: Rue du Commerce arcades at dawn
walks:Rue du Commerce arcades at dawn.label: WALLS
walks:Rue du Commerce arcades at dawn.hook: 20 min · 146 m of medieval arcades, Franche-Comté's only such street
walks:Rue du Commerce arcades at dawn.text: 20 min · 146 m of medieval arcades, Franche-Comté's only such street Walk the 146 m of golden-stone arcades early. Past number 24, Rouget de Lisle's birth house. Past Pâtisserie Pelen (since 1899). Out to Place de la Liberté and Bartholdi's statue. The town at its most quiet.

walks:Château-Chalon vineyard walk.name: Château-Chalon vineyard walk
walks:Château-Chalon vineyard walk.label: VINEYARD
walks:Château-Chalon vineyard walk.hook: 2 h · the hilltop village + the AOC parcels
walks:Château-Chalon vineyard walk.text: 2 h · the hilltop village + the AOC parcels Park at Château-Chalon village (15 km east of Lons), perched on a karst cliff. Walk up to the belvedere for the view east over the Bresse plain. Then descend through the Vin Jaune parcels of the Macle, Berthet-Bondet and Berthet-Bondet domaines on the blue-marl slope. Under 20 km of slope link Arbois, Pupillin and Château-Chalon — but the Château-Chalon AOC is the most concentrated 50 ha in France.

walks:Arbois old town + Pasteur lab.name: Arbois old town + Pasteur lab
walks:Arbois old town + Pasteur lab.label: TOWN
walks:Arbois old town + Pasteur lab.hook: Half-day · the wine capital's narrow streets, the lab at 83 rue de Courcelles
walks:Arbois old town + Pasteur lab.text: Half-day · the wine capital's narrow streets, the lab at 83 rue de Courcelles Park at the Place de la Liberté in Arbois. Walk past the 18th-c. arcades, down to the Cuisance and the bridge, past the Caveau d'Arbois cellar church and on to Maison de Louis Pasteur at 83 rue de Courcelles. Lunch at Le Bistronôme or Le Bistrot des Claquets .

walks:Baume-les-Messieurs cirque + abbey.name: Baume-les-Messieurs cirque + abbey
walks:Baume-les-Messieurs cirque + abbey.label: ABBEY
walks:Baume-les-Messieurs cirque + abbey.hook: 2-3 h · 9th-c. abbey under a karst amphitheatre
walks:Baume-les-Messieurs cirque + abbey.text: 2-3 h · 9th-c. abbey under a karst amphitheatre 15 km east of Lons. Walk the cirque trail to the source of the Dard from grottoes (~90 min). Then the village + Benedictine abbey (founded 869, Flemish polyptych). One of France's Plus Beaux Villages.

walks:Cascades du Hérisson — seven casca.name: Cascades du Hérisson — seven cascades
walks:Cascades du Hérisson — seven casca.label: WATERFALLS
walks:Cascades du Hérisson — seven casca.text: 3-4 h round trip · 65-m + 60-m falls Seven waterfalls along 3.5 km of trail, rising 255 m. Park at Doucier. L'Éventail (65 m) is the first; Le Grand Saut (60 m) the climax. Best in spring after snowmelt. Hat, boots, water.

walks:Belvédère des Quatre Lacs.name: Belvédère des Quatre Lacs
walks:Belvédère des Quatre Lacs.label: VIEW
walks:Belvédère des Quatre Lacs.hook: 1 h · view over four glacial lakes from a single ridge
walks:Belvédère des Quatre Lacs.text: 1 h · view over four glacial lakes from a single ridge A short climb on the Frasnois plateau (35 km east of Lons) reaches the Belvédère des Quatre Lacs — a single ridge view down over Lac d'Ilay, Lac du Petit Maclu, Lac du Grand Maclu and Lac de Narlay, four glacial lakes left by the last ice age. The hike continues to the Pic de l'Aigle (60 min more).

secret-gems:Cour Rouget de Lisle — the t.name: Cour Rouget de Lisle — the tilleul at 14:00 in May
secret-gems:Cour Rouget de Lisle — the t.label: GEM
secret-gems:Cour Rouget de Lisle — the t.text: The courtyard of Rouget de Lisle's birth house (1760) holds an ancient lime tree. At 14:00 in May the bells of the Cordeliers, Saint-Désiré and the Hôpital sound together — three timbres, seconds apart. Almost always empty. Where 24 rue du Commerce When 14:00 in May (tilleul in flower)

secret-gems:Source Salée — Parc des Bain.name: Source Salée — Parc des Bains, 07:30 brume
secret-gems:Source Salée — Parc des Bain.label: GEM
secret-gems:Source Salée — Parc des Bain.text: Bassin de la Source Salée, free access. At 7:30 on a September morning, brume rises from the deep brine. Water still near 300 g/L — you can taste it. The etymological origin of Lons-le-Saunier (saunier = salt-worker), right there in the pool. Where Parc des Bains When 07:30 September-November

secret-gems:Saint-Désiré crypt — Merovin.name: Saint-Désiré crypt — Merovingian sarcophagus
secret-gems:Saint-Désiré crypt — Merovin.label: GEM
secret-gems:Saint-Désiré crypt — Merovin.text: The 11th-century Romanesque church has a 6th-century Merovingian stone sarcophagus of Saint Désiré in the crypt. The keeper opens it on request. The earliest material layer of the town. Where Lons centre When morning hours, ask the keeper

secret-gems:The Cuisance bank in Arbois.name: The Cuisance bank in Arbois — late afternoon
secret-gems:The Cuisance bank in Arbois.label: GEM
secret-gems:The Cuisance bank in Arbois.text: Walk down from Place de la Liberté to the Cuisance bridge. The river runs clear; the Cuisance trout still spawn here. The terrace of Le Bistronôme backs onto this river — early in the season the swallows feed on rising flies. Where Arbois — banks of the Cuisance river When 16:30-18:00

secret-gems:Château-Chalon belvedere at.name: Château-Chalon belvedere at sunset
secret-gems:Château-Chalon belvedere at.label: GEM
secret-gems:Château-Chalon belvedere at.text: Park at the village entry. Walk to the belvedere east of the church. The Bresse plain stretches west; the blue-marl Vin Jaune parcels drop away at your feet. In late September the light turns the slope amber — sotolon-coloured, before the cellars start producing it. Where Château-Chalon hilltop When 60 min before sunset

street-food:Saucisse de Morteau IGP from.name: Saucisse de Morteau IGP from the market
street-food:Saucisse de Morteau IGP from.label: STREET FOOD
street-food:Saucisse de Morteau IGP from.text: A tuyé-smoked Morteau IGP straight from a producer truck, gently simmered (never pierced) for 45 minutes when you get home. Some market vendors will serve a hot slice with bread and mustard for €5. The Jura's most direct quick eat. Where Place du 11 Novembre When Thursday + Saturday mornings

street-food:Warm gougères from the boula.name: Warm gougères from the boulangerie
street-food:Warm gougères from the boula.label: STREET FOOD
street-food:Warm gougères from the boula.text: Cheese choux puffs made with Comté — the Jura's apéro bite. Bought warm from any good Lons boulangerie. Eat them on the rue du Commerce arcades before they cool. Where rue du Commerce + Pelen When Saturday morning

street-food:Cancoillotte by the jar — to.name: Cancoillotte by the jar — to take home
street-food:Cancoillotte by the jar — to.label: STREET FOOD
street-food:Cancoillotte by the jar — to.text: The Franche-Comté peasant cheese — under 15 % fat, melted from metton with garlic and Jura white wine. Sold cold in glass jars; warmed at home and poured over potatoes. The cheese that almost no one outside the region knows at its best. Where all markets + fromageries When any opening

gastronomy:Thursday market — the big one.name: Thursday market — the big one
gastronomy:Thursday market — the big one.label: MARKET
gastronomy:Thursday market — the big one.hook: All Thursday · the biggest market in the Jura department
gastronomy:Thursday market — the big one.text: All Thursday · the biggest market in the Jura department Place du 11 Novembre (manufactured goods all day) + Place de Verdun (food morning). Producers from the Haut-Jura plateau and the Bresse plain. Saucisse de Morteau IGP from a tuyé producer, three ages of Comté, cancoillotte by the jar, Mont d'Or in season, miel de sapin, Bleu de Gex. Where Place du 11 Novembre + Place de Verdun

gastronomy:Saturday market — Cours Sully.name: Saturday market — Cours Sully
gastronomy:Saturday market — Cours Sully.label: MARKET
gastronomy:Saturday market — Cours Sully.text: Saturday morning · food only The smaller weekend market — food and table goods only, quieter, more local. For a calm shop and a sit-down at the Café de la Comédie afterwards. Where Cours Sully (Lons centre)

gastronomy:Domaine Macle — Château-Chalo.name: Domaine Macle — Château-Chalon
gastronomy:Domaine Macle — Château-Chalo.label: WINE — VIN JAUNE
gastronomy:Domaine Macle — Château-Chalo.hook: The canonical Château-Chalon · family settled 1850 · 8th gen 2025
gastronomy:Domaine Macle — Château-Chalo.text: The canonical Château-Chalon · family settled 1850 · 8th gen 2025 Family in Château-Chalon since 1850. Laurent Macle has run the estate since 1995 (7th gen); his daughter Carmen Macle joined in January 2025 as 8th gen. 12 ha: 8 ha Chardonnay in Côtes du Jura + 4 ha Savagnin in Château-Chalon. Visits by appointment only. The reference Vin Jaune house — wines of extraordinary purity and longevity. Château-Chalon declassified vintages: 1974, 1980, 1984, 2001. Where Château-Chalon (30 km east-north) Address Rue de la Roche, 39210 Château-Chalon Phone +33 3 84 85 21 85

gastronomy:Domaine Stéphane Tissot.name: Domaine Stéphane Tissot
gastronomy:Domaine Stéphane Tissot.label: WINE — BIODYNAMIC
gastronomy:Domaine Stéphane Tissot.text: 50 ha · Demeter biodynamic since 2004 · 30+ cuvées Bénédicte & Stéphane Tissot, 50 ha — one of the Jura's largest serious estates. Organic 1999, biodynamic Demeter 2004. Over 30 cuvées on blue and grey marls, limestone and clay — across all five principal Jura varieties. Practices sous-voile ageing for certain Savagnin and Chardonnay wines. Tissot vines surround Pasteur's experimental vineyard plot in Montigny-lès-Arsures — the same village. Where Montigny-lès-Arsures (Arbois) Address 39 Rue de Curon, 39600 Montigny-lès-Arsures Phone +33 3 84 66 08 27

gastronomy:Maison Pierre Overnoy / Emman.name: Maison Pierre Overnoy / Emmanuel Houillon — Pupillin
gastronomy:Maison Pierre Overnoy / Emman.label: WINE — NATURAL
gastronomy:Maison Pierre Overnoy / Emman.hook: The natural-wine reference of the Jura · sulfur-free since 1984
gastronomy:Maison Pierre Overnoy / Emman.text: The natural-wine reference of the Jura · sulfur-free since 1984 Pierre Overnoy embraced sulfur-free winemaking in 1984, earning the title "pope of natural wine." Emmanuel Houillon (Overnoy's protégé and son-in-law) took over running of the domaine in 2001, with Overnoy continuing in an advisory role. 6 ha, equally divided between Ploussard, Chardonnay, Savagnin. Certified biodynamic. Allocation-only. A Pupillin Ploussard from Overnoy/Houillon is among the most sought-after natural wines in the world. The village is opposite La Table du Grapiot ★. Where Pupillin Address 32 rue du Ploussard, 39600 Pupillin Phone +33 3 84 66 24 27

gastronomy:Domaine Jean-François Ganevat.name: Domaine Jean-François Ganevat — Rotalier
gastronomy:Domaine Jean-François Ganevat.label: WINE — CULT
gastronomy:Domaine Jean-François Ganevat.hook: 14th generation since 1650 · 25 grape varieties on 9 ha · sulfur-free since 2006
gastronomy:Domaine Jean-François Ganevat.text: 14th generation since 1650 · 25 grape varieties on 9 ha · sulfur-free since 2006 Jean-François Ganevat returned in 1998 from Burgundy (Jean-Marc Morey, Chassagne-Montrachet) to a 14th-generation family domaine. 9 ha, 25 grape varieties including rare indigenous types. Organic; eliminated sulfur in the cellar by 2006. Over 40 single-parcel cuvées; a négoce label with his sister Anne. Allocation-only; cult status internationally. Where Rotalier (southern Côtes du Jura, 25 km south of Lons) Address Lieu-dit La Combe, 39190 Rotalier

gastronomy:Marcel Petite — Fort Saint-An.name: Marcel Petite — Fort Saint-Antoine affinage
gastronomy:Marcel Petite — Fort Saint-An.label: CHEESE
gastronomy:Marcel Petite — Fort Saint-An.hook: 100,000 Comté wheels aging in a 19th-c. military fort
gastronomy:Marcel Petite — Fort Saint-An.text: 100,000 Comté wheels aging in a 19th-c. military fort Built 1879–1882 as part of the Séré de Rivières defensive system. In 1966, affineur Marcel Petite began renting it to age Comté in cold, slow, mountain conditions — 6–9 °C and 94–98 % humidity. Approximately 100,000 wheels age there at any time, on spruce shelves, for 10–20 months. Since 1966, over one million wheels have passed through the fort. Visits possible during summer; cheese available at the Maison du Comté and major fromageries (look for the dark-blue "Marcel Petite" label). Where Fort Saint-Antoine, near Pontarlier (1,100 m altitude) Address Fort Saint-Antoine, 25160 Saint-Antoine (near Pontarlier)

gastronomy:Volaille Miéral — Bresse AOP.name: Volaille Miéral — Bresse AOP
gastronomy:Volaille Miéral — Bresse AOP.label: POULTRY
gastronomy:Volaille Miéral — Bresse AOP.hook: The reference Bresse-poultry house — supplier to the starred Jura tables
gastronomy:Volaille Miéral — Bresse AOP.text: The reference Bresse-poultry house — supplier to the starred Jura tables Bresse AOP poultry from the Miéral house — Bresse chickens, capons, pintades. 'Blue legs,' four-month feeding regime, supplier to Maison Jeunet, Mont Joly, and beyond. The poularde for the cathedral dish. Sous-vide for the boat possible. Order 48 h ahead in season. Where Montrevel-en-Bresse (50 min west of Lons) Address Place de la Grenette, 01340 Montrevel-en-Bresse Phone +33 4 74 25 48 36

gastronomy:Fromagerie Vagne — Lons.name: Fromagerie Vagne — Lons
gastronomy:Fromagerie Vagne — Lons.label: FROMAGER
gastronomy:Fromagerie Vagne — Lons.hook: Fromager-affineur · three ages of Comté side by side
gastronomy:Fromagerie Vagne — Lons.text: Fromager-affineur · three ages of Comté side by side Central Lons fromagerie-affineur: 18 / 24 / 36-month Comté side by side, Bleu de Gex, Morbier, Mont d'Or in season, cancoillotte. Ask for the comparative plate. Sous-vide for the boat possible. Where rue du Commerce (arcades) Address rue du Commerce, 39000 Lons-le-Saunier

gastronomy:Pâtisserie Chocolaterie Pelen.name: Pâtisserie Chocolaterie Pelen
gastronomy:Pâtisserie Chocolaterie Pelen.label: PASTRY
gastronomy:Pâtisserie Chocolaterie Pelen.text: Since 1899 · Galet de Chalain (praliné-nougatine, 1984) Maison since 1899. Arnaud Pelen, 4th gen. Bean-to-bar chocolate roasted in-house. The Galet de Chalain — nougatine shell + almond-hazelnut praline + cocoa coating, created by Dominique Pelen in 1984 and named for the Néolithique-lacustre Lac de Chalain — is the souvenir comestible. Where 175 rue Blaise Pascal Address 175 rue Blaise Pascal, 39000 Lons-le-Saunier

avoid:Looking for Jeunet at 9 rue de l'H.name: Looking for Jeunet at 9 rue de l'Hôtel de Ville in Arbois
avoid:Looking for Jeunet at 9 rue de l'H.label: AVOID
avoid:Looking for Jeunet at 9 rue de l'H.hook: The historic address has been closed since Jean-Paul Jeunet's retirement
avoid:Looking for Jeunet at 9 rue de l'H.text: The historic address has been closed since Jean-Paul Jeunet's retirement Jean-Paul Jeunet retired; Steven Naessens took the name and the two stars to the Château de Germigney in Port-Lesney in November 2021. The old Arbois address at 9 rue de l'Hôtel de Ville no longer operates as a starred restaurant. Many guides (including the previous version of this one) still send readers there. The current address is Maison Jeunet par Steven Naessens, 31 rue Edgar Faure, 39600 Port-Lesney .

avoid:\"Vin Jaune\" tasting on a Place d.name: "Vin Jaune" tasting on a Place de la Liberté terrace
avoid:\"Vin Jaune\" tasting on a Place d.label: AVOID
avoid:\"Vin Jaune\" tasting on a Place d.hook: Real Vin Jaune is tasted at the producer's, not under the arcades
avoid:\"Vin Jaune\" tasting on a Place d.text: Real Vin Jaune is tasted at the producer's, not under the arcades If the bottle on the terrace is 75 cl, it isn't Vin Jaune — Vin Jaune is mandatorily 62 cl clavelin , the format is legally protected. Several centre-town "dégustation" cellars in Lons and Arbois pour topped-up oxidative Savagnin under the name and charge tourist prices. Real Vin Jaune is tasted at the winemaker's: Macle in Château-Chalon, Tissot in Montigny, or at the Caveau des Jacobins in Lons. The 62 cl clavelin is the proof of identity.

avoid:Industrial \"Comté\" at a tourist.name: Industrial "Comté" at a tourist cellar
avoid:Industrial \"Comté\" at a tourist.label: AVOID
avoid:Industrial \"Comté\" at a tourist.hook: Three ages side by side, or it's not the real lesson
avoid:Industrial \"Comté\" at a tourist.text: Three ages side by side, or it's not the real lesson Cellars selling pre-cut Comté in plastic at €25/kg are selling young, mass-affined wheels. Real Comté differentiates radically by age and affineur — Marcel Petite's Fort Saint-Antoine wheels at 24+ months are a different cheese from a 12-month industrial wheel. Buy from a real fromager-affineur — Fromagerie Vagne on rue du Commerce, or at the Thursday market — and taste three ages side by side before deciding.

avoid:\"Pasteur defended his thesis on V.name: "Pasteur defended his thesis on Vin Jaune"
avoid:\"Pasteur defended his thesis on V.label: AVOID
avoid:\"Pasteur defended his thesis on V.hook: Honest correction — the 1857 paper was on lactic fermentation
avoid:\"Pasteur defended his thesis on V.text: Honest correction — the 1857 paper was on lactic fermentation A widely repeated story says Pasteur defended his doctoral thesis on the fermentation of Pupillin's Vin Jaune. The reality: his doctorate (1847) was on crystallography (tartaric-acid optical asymmetry). The 1857 work was a Mémoire sur la fermentation appelée lactique , read at the Académie des Sciences on 30 November 1857 — establishing that lactic fermentation is the work of living microorganisms. The Arbois work on wine spoilage that gave us pasteurisation came later. The myth blurs the timeline; the actual achievement is no less. Microbiology genuinely began at the foot of Jura barrels — just not as a doctoral thesis.
